stem: Meher's four quiz scores are 6, 8, 10, and 12. Their mean is 9. Every score is then multiplied by 3.

parts.text: Which claim about the new mean is correct?

options.text: The new mean is $9\times3=27$, because every value was multiplied by 3.
The old mean 9 is what creates the multiplier 3, rather than scaling the mean by 3.
Multiply only the score 12 by 3 and keep mean 9, as if one value were enough.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: When every value is multiplied by the same fixed number, the mean is multiplied by that number too.

teacher.key_rationale: Scaling every value by 3 scales the mean by 3. Saying the mean creates the multiplier reverses the relation. Scaling only one value drops the every-value condition.
